claims.text: High-temperature wear resistance of FeNiCrCoCu coatings is governed by oxide-layer stability.
Oxide-layer stability depends on alloy composition.
A continuous, adherent, protective oxide scale improves wear resistance during high-temperature sliding.
Increasing Cr content by 10% relative to the baseline will enhance oxide-scale formation.
The Cr-enhanced coating will form a continuous, adherent, Cr-rich oxide layer during wear.
Increasing Cr content promotes formation of a Cr2O3-rich oxide layer.
The Cr2O3-rich oxide layer is thermodynamically stable at 600–800°C.
The Cr2O3-rich layer reduces direct metal-to-metal contact.
The Cr2O3-rich layer reduces oxidation-driven material loss.
The Cr-enhanced coating will have at least a 30% lower wear rate than the baseline coating under the specified conditions.
The proposed applicability range is 600–800°C and normal loads up to 10 N.
The hypothesis may not apply outside the stated temperature and load range or to coatings with drastically different microstructures.
Cr enrichment may fail to stabilize the oxide layer or may compromise other mechanical properties.
A wear-rate improvement of less than 10%, or failure to form a stable, continuous Cr-rich layer, is designated as a falsifying result.

contradictions.description: The prediction requires at least a 30% wear-rate reduction, but the falsification rule only rejects improvements below 10%. Outcomes between 10% and 30% would violate the quantitative prediction without falsifying the hypothesis under the stated rule.
